第 61 章 Onboard People, Not Technology让人入职，不是让技术入职

Marcus Blankenship / 马库斯·布兰肯希普

— 第 175 页 —

At my first programming job, it took three weeks to get my dev environment fully set up. I was only the second developer to work at the company, ever, so nothing was documented. The first person quit, which is why I had the job. At my second job, it took only four days because I was the eighth person in the programming department, so I had seven other people to help me. Today, my clients tell me things like, "we use Docker, so it takes less than an hour to onboard a new developer." I'm glad new devs don't need to face the same frustrations that I did. But setting up a productive dev environment isn't onboarding. Onboarding is setting up a person to work productively on your team.

在我第一份编程工作中，花了三周才完全搭好开发环境。我是公司有史以来第二个开发者，所以什么都没文档化。第一个人辞职了，这就是我有工作的原因。在第二份工作中，只花了四天，因为我是编程部第八个人，所以有七个人帮我。今天，我的客户告诉我「我们用 Docker，所以入职新开发者不到一小时」。我很高兴新开发者不用面对我经历的同样挫折。但搭好高效开发环境不是入职。入职是让一个人准备好在你的团队高效工作。

A Leadership Smell一种领导异味

Some managers might fall into the trap of believing that after they're done setting up the dev environment, they've done their part to make the new developer successful and that the rest is up to the new employee, that all they need is a computer, a chair, a dev environment, and a project to work on. This is a dangerous leadership smell. Dangerous for the manager, yes, but mostly for the new developer. The danger is the unspoken idea that after we apply onboarding to a new developer, they have everything they need to be productive. Of course, when you read it, it seems sort of ridiculous. But I get a whiff of this from managers at many organizations I work with. It typically comes out in a conversation like this:

有些经理可能陷入陷阱，认为搭好开发环境后，他们已经尽了自己的部分让新开发者成功，剩下的就靠新员工了，他们只需要一台电脑、一把椅子、一个开发环境、一个项目做。这是一种危险的领导异味。对经理危险，是的，但主要对新开发者危险。危险在于一个没说出口的想法：我们对新开发者做了入职后，他们就有了高效工作所需的一切。当然，你读起来觉得有点荒谬。但我从我合作的很多组织的经理那里闻到这个味道。它通常在这样的对话中出现：

Me: How is your new programmer working out? Manager: He's doing…okay. Not quite what I hoped, but he'll be fine.

我：你的新程序员怎么样？经理：他……还行。不太是我希望的那样，但他会好的。

— 第 176 页 —

Me: What makes you say that? Manager: Well, we got everything set up quickly, and we got him all his access and onboarding. But he's just a lot slower than I expected. Me: Why did you expect he'd be faster? Manager: First, he was supposed to be an expert in Java development. Second, we've automated our dev environment setup at great cost and effort. So, there shouldn't be anything standing in his way.

我：为什么这么说？经理：我们很快把一切都搭好了，给了他所有权限和入职。但他就是比我预期慢很多。我：你为什么预期他会更快？经理：首先，他本应是 Java 开发专家。其次，我们花了很大代价和精力自动化了开发环境搭建。所以应该没什么挡他路。

As you might guess, this situation is more dangerous for the programmer than the manager, because it's the manager's expectations that aren't being met. It's the manager who's disappointed by the speed at which things are progressing. And it's the manager who feels that their onboarding process, whatever it is, should yield a developer that's "up to speed and ready to run." So, if the manager believes they've done their part, the problem must be with the developer's motivation, drive, or skill. This ignores the most important keys to productivity: good relationships and a healthy environment. These are the things your developer needs to be onboarded to, and it takes much longer than just a few hours.

你可能猜到，这个情况对程序员比对经理更危险，因为是经理的期望没被满足。是经理对事情进展速度失望。是经理觉得他们的入职流程，不管是什么，应该产出一个「上手准备好跑」的开发者。所以如果经理认为他们尽了自己的部分，问题一定在开发者的动机、内驱力或技能上。这忽视了生产力最重要的关键：好关系和健康环境。这些才是你的开发者需要被入职进去的东西，而且它花的时间远不止几小时。

Onboarding Is Leading入职是领导

Onboarding is a key activity of technical managers and leaders. It's not the responsibility of HR, and it's certainly not simply setting up the dev environment. In my experience, onboarding should include or result in the following:

入职是技术经理和领导的关键活动。它不是 HR 的责任，当然也不只是搭好开发环境。根据我的经验，入职应该包括或带来以下：

  • Positive relationships with the developer's team和开发者团队的积极关系
  • Introductions to the project stakeholders向项目利益相关者介绍
  • Clarity about the team's current goals清楚团队当前目标
  • Knowledge of key upcoming projects了解关键的即将到来的项目
  • Clarity about the team's values清楚团队价值观
  • Knowing who to go to for help and how often it's okay to ask for help知道找谁求助、多久求助一次可以
  • Firsthand experience with the team's development process and ceremonies (Agile, Scrum, standups, retros, etc.)亲身体验团队的开发流程和仪式（敏捷、Scrum、站会、回顾会等）
  • Firsthand experience with the key communication channels (team meetings, one-on-ones, etc.)亲身体验关键沟通渠道（团队会议、一对一等）
— 第 177 页 —
  • Receiving a piece of adjusting and affirming feedback from their manager从经理那里收到一条调整和肯定的反馈
  • Giving a piece of adjusting and affirming feedback to their manager and teammates给经理和队友一条调整和肯定的反馈
  • A clear sense of the tech and infrastructure used by the team清楚团队用的技术和基础设施
  • A working dev environment可用的开发环境

How Long Should This Take?这需要多久？

It should take you, the manager, at least a few weeks to initially onboard a new developer. After that, expect it to take a few quarters (three to nine months) for a new developer to "come up to speed." Of course, this will vary wildly according to the kind of projects you are working on. I've led teams where I spent a year onboarding a dev to work on a large ERP system. You might have experienced even longer. Onboarding is important leadership work that you need to be actively involved with. Like other work, you don't need to do it all yourself, but you need to make sure it all gets done—and done well. Onboarding sets the stage for many years of productive work. Don't shortchange your team by pretending it's just about tools, paperwork, or diversity videos. It's about intentionally getting the proper relationships in place from day one, which is the key to productive development teams.

你作为经理初步入职一个新开发者应该花至少几周。之后，预期新开发者需要几个季度（三到九个月）才能「上手」。当然，这会根据你做的项目类型差异很大。我领导过团队，我花了一年时间入职一个开发者在大型 ERP 系统上工作。你可能经历过更长。入职是重要的领导工作，你需要积极参与。像其他工作一样，你不需要全自己做，但你需要确保都完成——并且做好。入职为多年的高效工作搭舞台。不要假装它只是工具、文书或多元化视频来亏待你的团队。它是关于从第一天起有意识地建立合适的关系，这是高效开发团队的关键。
